nodes.text: Pathophysiology: severe atherosclerotic stenosis of proximal subclavian artery causes retrograde vertebral flow to supply exercising arm
Clinical presentation: exercise-induced ipsilateral arm claudication + vertebrobasilar insufficiency (dizziness, vertigo, diplopia) + BP differential > 15 mm Hg
Noninvasive diagnostic imaging: duplex ultrasound demonstrating retrograde flow in ipsilateral vertebral artery and blunted subclavian waveforms
Confirmatory vascular imaging: CT angiography or MR angiography of the chest and neck to map stenosis anatomy
Revascularization for symptomatic disease: percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with stent placement across proximal subclavian stenosis
**Long-segment or anatomically unfavorable occlusion:** carotid-subclavian surgical bypass grafting

algorithm.title: Surrogate consent hierarchy and organ donation

nodes.text: Confirm brain death: legally and clinically dead following formal apnea testing and absent brainstem reflexes
Determine donor status: review state donor registry or driver license for prior documented first-person authorization
**Documented first-person authorization:** proceed with organ procurement organization without requiring family consent
Identify highest-ranking legally competent surrogate: spouse, adult children, parents, or adult siblings in statutory order
**No legally competent adult surrogate available (minor sibling):** obtain emergency court-appointed guardian authorization
Contact local organ procurement organization to coordinate logistics and donor organ preservation

nodes.text: Identify situational trigger: prolonged motionless standing (church choir), warm room, or emotional distress
Characteristic presentation: brief loss of consciousness (< 1 minute) without postictal confusion or focal neurologic deficits
Rule out cardiogenic syncope: normal 12-lead ECG + absence of structural heart disease, family sudden death, or exertional onset
Provide patient reassurance regarding the benign physiological nature of vasovagal reflex syncope
Educate on physical counterpressure maneuvers: leg crossing, hand grip, and arm tensing at prodrome onset
Maintain adequate oral hydration and sodium intake + avoid prolonged unmoving standing

Emergent noncontrast head CT: hyperdense subarachnoid blood in basal cisterns and sulci

Definitive aneurysm securing: emergent endovascular coiling or microsurgical clipping within 24 hours

nodes.text: Recognize clinical presentation: fatigable ptosis worsening with sustained upward gaze + variable binocular diplopia + evening fatigue
Perform bedside diagnostic testing: positive ice pack test (ptosis improves after 2 minutes) or edrophonium test
Repetitive nerve stimulation study demonstrating decremental compound motor action potential (> 10%)
Serologic testing: serum acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibodies + muscle-specific kinase (MuSK) antibodies
Initiate first-line symptomatic therapy: oral pyridostigmine (acetylcholinesterase inhibitor) to improve transmission
Order chest CT without contrast to screen for thymoma or thymic hyperplasia
